name: LLM gateway: wybór modelu
description: Whether the model can route a user request to the right model tier (small, large, code, web search or human).
instructions: Which model tier should handle this request?

criteria.small_model: Short, simple tasks: greetings, quick stable facts, rephrasing, short translation, simple formatting
criteria.large_model: Multi-step reasoning, long documents, analysis, planning, nuanced writing or advice without code
criteria.code_model: Writing, fixing, explaining or reviewing source code, SQL, regex, shell scripts, configs
criteria.web_search: Needs current information: news, prices, rates, weather, schedules, recent releases, live status
criteria.human_handoff: Needs a human: account-specific actions, legal or medical emergencies, explicit request to talk to a person, complaints

state.request:
Context from our product doc (v0.3):

Bookly is a booking tool for small physiotherapy clinics. Each clinic has several therapists; each therapist has a weekly availability template (e.g. Mon 8-14, Wed 12-18) and ad-hoc exceptions (holidays, sick days). Patients book visits of a given service type (consultation 30 min, therapy 50 min, massage 60 min). A visit has a status: booked, confirmed, cancelled_by_patient, cancelled_by_clinic, no_show, done. Clinics want to see no-show rates per patient and per therapist. A patient can belong to multiple clinics (franchise), but clinical notes must never be visible across clinics. Payments are out of scope for v1, but leave room for a visit price snapshot (price can change over time, the visit keeps the price from booking time). Audit: every status change must keep who changed it and when.

We've discussed the product side to death already, so I don't need opinions on the business model or the roadmap. Please give me the PostgreSQL schema: CREATE TABLE statements with keys, constraints and indexes that support the no-show reports, plus a short comment on how the status history table works.
